elements.element: Customer may terminate on 60–90 days' notice (fallback notice right)
elements.evidence: "unless terminated by either Party hereto upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other" — this operates only as notice of non-renewal at each anniversary; no mid-term convenience right for the Company is created, yet (a) now presupposes one ("terminates this Agreement for convenience prior to the end of the then-current term").

elements.element: Early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees
elements.evidence: "in no event shall the Termination Payment exceed the aggregate payments made by the Company to HDI pursuant to Section 3.1 in respect of the three (3) months immediately preceding the Termination Date"

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term
elements.evidence: "automatically renewed for an additional one year period on each anniversary ... unless terminated by either Party" — HDI's right arises only at the renewal point.

elements.element: Vendor's end-of-term convenience termination requires 90 days' notice
elements.evidence: "upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other"

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice
elements.evidence: Only "ninety (90) days written notice" at each anniversary; no 30-day right.

elements.element: Pro-rata refund of prepaid fees on Customer termination
elements.evidence: No refund language anywhere in Section 4.1; only a "Termination Payment" payable by the Company.

elements.element: Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term
elements.evidence: "terminated by either Party hereto upon ninety (90) days written notice" operates only as non-renewal at an anniversary.

offending_extra_words: for convenience prior to the end of the then-current term

No Termination Payment shall be due or payable where the Company terminates this Agreement by notice of non-renewal under Section 4.1, pursuant to Section 1.6, or by reason of HDI's breach of this Agreement.
reasons: The fee cap is correctly set at three months' payments to HDI for the three months preceding the Termination Date, so that fallback element is satisfied.

The fallback still fails on the Customer's termination right: the redline conditions the Termination Payment on termination "for convenience prior to the end of the then-current term", but no such mid-term convenience right is granted anywhere, leaving a dangling mechanic and no 60–90 day convenience termination for the Company.

Minimality gate failed: the operation expands 55 words to 134 (ratio 2.44). The three-month cap could be inserted as a short proviso; the added non-renewal / Section 1.6 / HDI-breach carve-outs are separate protections beyond what the fallback fee cap requires.
The Section 1.6 and breach carve-outs also import protection from a different bargain (avoiding an exit fee where Vendor is at fault) rather than completing the locked fallback level.
